name: Vikram Solar Ltd
tagline: Solar module manufacturer riding India's 10-year renewable energy tailwind; strong growth, improving quality metrics, but working-capital heavy and stock down 53% YTD
business_overview: Vikram Solar manufactures advanced solar PV modules (monocrystalline, bifacial, HJT, N-type; 395-735W range) and provides EPC and O&M services. Incorporated in 2005, operates one of India's oldest and largest solar cell/module manufacturing facilities. Positioned as a China+1 alternative for solar infrastructure buildout.
fundamentals_narrative: Revenue growth strong (32% 3Y CAGR, 33% TTM) with profit growth even stronger (65% 5Y CAGR, 44% TTM), reflecting both volume scaling and margin expansion as capacity utilization improves. ROE 21.4% and ROCE 30.6% are excellent for a manufacturer in a growth phase. Debt/Equity fell sharply to ~0.11 in Mar-2026 post-equity raise (issuance of Rs 362 Cr equity capital), reducing interest burden. Working capital and debtor days have both improved markedly, suggesting operational efficiency gains. However, recent quarterly deterioration (Q2 FY26: net profit Rs 20 Cr vs Rs 110 Cr in Mar-2026) signals cyclical/project-mix pressure or module price weakness in Sep-Oct 2026 quarter.
technical_read: Stock has crashed 53% in 1 year (Rs 355 high in Oct 2025 to Rs 154 Oct 2026), far outpacing the Nifty decline. Recent quarters show volatile earnings (Q2 FY26 PAT only Rs 20 Cr on Rs 1,563 Cr sales, 1.3% margin, vs Mar-2026's 16% margin). Stock is near 52-week lows; technical bounce possible but needs earnings recovery to sustain.
sentiment_summary: No direct ValuePickr thread found during scan (this is a web-discovery stock from broader solar sector tailwind conversation). Market consensus views VSL as a legitimate module-manufacturing play with scale and tech credentials, but concerns persist over (1) pricing power amid Chinese competition/module price deflation, (2) capex intensity for capacity additions (equipment costs remain high), (3) project-dependent earnings volatility. Recent Aug-Sep 2026 period saw VSL win 400 MW module supply (Maharashtra) and 1 GW supply deal with Avaada Electro (cell supply), suggesting order visibility, but Q2 margin collapse questions execution.
community_signal: Not tracked via ValuePickr forum. Market signal: strong order book (400 MW + 1 GW deals announced Sep 2026) but margin pressure evident in Q2 results. Promoter confidence is moderate (63% holding intact; no unusual transactions flagged).
bse_notes: Credit ratings upgraded: Fitch upgraded to A (from A-) in Aug 2026; SMERA upgraded to 'A' (from A-) in Sep 2025. Indicates improving financial profile and bank comfort. No SEBI action found.
bull_case: India's renewable energy capacity target (500 GW by 2030) creates massive TAM; solar CAGR estimated 15-20% through 2030
Company is scaling toward 10+ GW module manufacturing capacity; recent deals (400 MW module supply, 1 GW cell supply) signal traction
ROCE 30.6% and ROE 21.4% are strong; working capital and debtor-day improvements show operational leverage kicking in
Mar-2026 equity raise cleaned up balance sheet; D/E fell to 0.11x (one of the best in manufacturing)
Promoters committed (63% holding) and management has execution track record since 2005 IPO in 2015 via DRHP
bear_case: Q2 FY26 earnings collapse (net profit Rs 20 Cr vs Rs 110 Cr in Mar-2026) suggests severe margin compression or project-mix issue — solar module prices globally deflating 5-10% YoY, squeezing OEMs
Stock down 53% YTD signals market skepticism on profitability sustainability; recent wins don't prevent Q2 miss
Module manufacturing capex heavy; equipment cost inflation (polysilicon cell equipment) remains a risk to margin expansion
Execution risk on capacity ramp (10 GW target ambitious given Q2 stumble); any production delays could extend recovery timeline
Debt refinancing cost elevated (interest Rs 178 Cr TTM on shrinking revenue base if FY27 guidance misses)
thesis_fit: 10x-in-2-3-years IF margins recover and capex converts to profitable capacity; otherwise neither
verdict_headline: Solar module manufacturer with real TAM and improving balance sheet but facing near-term margin pressure — await Q3 FY27 recovery signals before conviction
verdict_reasoning: Fundamentals are compelling (ROCE 31%, ROE 21%, debt-free post equity raise, 32% revenue CAGR) for a 10x story IF the company can defend module margins amid global deflation
Q2 margin collapse is a serious red flag that execution/pricing power is weaker than the 2020-2025 build phase suggested
Order book visibility (400 MW + 1 GW announced) gives hope FY27 Q3-Q4 may recover, but need to see it in results before raising conviction
Market is heavily discounting fear of continued pricing pressure; upside triggers: (a) stable ASP in Q3 results, (b) guidance for 25%+ FY27-28 profit growth, (c) 2-3 more GW deals announced

four_box.note: Tailwind (solar 10-yr capex cycle, India 500 GW target 2030) is strong 3.5/4. TAM (module supply for 50-100 GW annual Indian capex) is also large 3.5/4. Moat (2.5/4: manufacturing scale + tech portfolio real, but replicable; no pricing power vs Chinese competitors). Valuation (2.5/4: P/E 15.5x seems reasonable for 30%+ ROCE, but earnings volatile and stock down 53% YTD, suggesting more downside risk than upside from here). Composite: strong winds & TAM offset by moat gap and valuation uncertainty.
